items.q: The sickle mutation substitutes which amino acid at beta globin position six?
items.exp: Sickle haemoglobin replaces hydrophilic glutamate with hydrophobic valine at beta six, enabling polymerisation when deoxygenated. This single change drives the entire disease.
r: Correct. Valine replaces glutamate at position six.
Incorrect. Lysine substitution at six causes haemoglobin C disease.
Incorrect. The normal residue is glutamate, replaced by valine.
Incorrect. Histidine changes occur in other haemoglobin variants.
items.kp: Sickle: glutamate out, valine in, at beta six.

items.q: Which factor most directly inhibits HbS polymerisation and sickling?
o: High oxygen tension only in lungs
Fetal haemoglobin within the red cell
items.exp: Haemoglobin F interrupts HbS polymer growth, protecting newborns and mediating hydroxycarbamide benefit. Acidosis and raised 2,3 BPG promote deoxygenation and worsen sickling.
r: Incorrect. Oxygen helps but intracellular HbF is the direct inhibitor tested.
Correct. Fetal haemoglobin blocks polymerisation.
Incorrect. Raised 2,3 BPG favours deoxy HbS and sickling.
Incorrect. Low pH (Bohr effect) promotes sickling.
items.kp: HbF is nature and therapy against sickling.

items.q: Fever, chest pain, hypoxia and a new infiltrate in sickle cell disease define which emergency?
items.exp: Acute chest syndrome combines new pulmonary infiltrate with respiratory symptoms and is the leading cause of death in sickle cell disease. Infection, fat embolism and in situ sickling contribute.
r: Incorrect. Sequestration causes rapid anaemia with enlarging spleen.
Correct. New infiltrate plus chest symptoms means acute chest.
Incorrect. Aplastic crisis follows parvovirus with reticulocyte collapse.
Incorrect. Hyperhaemolysis follows transfusion reactions.
items.kp: Chest infiltrate in sickle disease is an emergency, not simple pneumonia alone.

items.q: Howell Jolly bodies in an older sickle cell child indicate what?
items.exp: Repeated splenic infarction destroys splenic filtering (autosplenectomy), so nuclear remnants persist as Howell Jolly bodies. Encapsulated organism sepsis risk rises sharply.
r: Incorrect. Iron deficiency does not produce these inclusions.
Correct. Howell Jolly bodies signal lost splenic function.
Incorrect. Recovery from B12 deficiency clears megaloblastic signs instead.
Incorrect. Lead causes basophilic stippling, not Howell Jolly bodies.
items.kp: Howell Jolly bodies mean the spleen no longer filters.

items.q: Beta thalassaemia trait is confirmed by which electrophoresis finding?
items.exp: Reduced beta chain production raises compensatory delta chain HbA2, so a raised HbA2 percentage confirms beta trait. Iron deficiency can lower HbA2 and mask it.
r: Incorrect. HbA2 is raised, not absent.
Correct. Raised HbA2 confirms beta trait.
Incorrect. HbS defines sickle states.
Incorrect. Hb Bart marks alpha thalassaemia hydrops.
items.kp: Beta trait proof is raised HbA2.

items.q: Four alpha gene deletions in a fetus produce which haemoglobin and outcome?
items.exp: Without alpha chains, gamma tetramers (haemoglobin Bart) cannot release oxygen to tissues, causing hydrops fetalis usually fatal without intrauterine transfusion.
r: Incorrect. Three deletions cause HbH disease.
Correct. Four deletions cause Bart hydrops.
Incorrect. Counts are profoundly abnormal.
Incorrect. Sickle disease is a beta chain disorder.
items.kp: Count alpha deletions: four is hydrops, three is HbH.

items.q: Parvovirus B19 infection in sickle cell disease causes which crisis?
items.exp: Parvovirus infects red cell precursors and halts production for days, catastrophic when red cell survival is already short, causing aplastic crisis with near zero reticulocytes.
r: Incorrect. Pain crises follow vaso occlusion, not marrow shutdown.
Correct. Parvovirus causes aplastic crisis.
Incorrect. Sequestration traps cells in the spleen with reticulocytosis.
Incorrect. Oxidant haemolysis typifies G6PD deficiency.
items.kp: Sickle plus parvovirus plus zero reticulocytes equals aplastic crisis.

items.q: Crew haircut skull appearance and chipmunk facies in thalassaemia major result from what?
items.exp: Massive erythroid hyperplasia expands marrow spaces, thinning cortex and producing hair on end skull trabeculae and maxillary overgrowth. Effective transfusion suppresses this expansion.
r: Incorrect. Iron loads soft organs, not marrow spaces this way.
Correct. Marrow expansion deforms the bones.
Incorrect. Rickets gives different metaphyseal changes.
Incorrect. Infection does not expand marrow symmetrically.
items.kp: Bone deformity in thalassaemia means unsuppressed marrow expansion.

items.q: The major cause of late death in transfused thalassaemia major without chelation is what?
items.exp: Transfusional iron deposits in myocardium causing fatal cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia without chelation. Cardiac MRI T2 star monitoring now guides chelation intensity.
r: Incorrect. Stroke dominates sickle disease risk instead.
Correct. Cardiac siderosis kills unchelated patients.
Incorrect. Acute chest is a sickle complication.
Incorrect. Stones are minor by comparison.
items.kp: In thalassaemia major, protect the iron loaded heart.

items.q: Hydroxycarbamide benefits sickle cell disease mainly by which action?
items.exp: Hydroxycarbamide raises haemoglobin F, which dilutes HbS and blocks polymerisation, reducing pain crises and acute chest events. It also lowers leukocytes and reticulocytes modestly.
r: Incorrect. Chelators treat iron overload in thalassaemia.
Correct. Raising HbF is the main benefit.
Incorrect. Antiplatelet action is not its mechanism.
Incorrect. It does not split formed polymers.
items.kp: Hydroxycarbamide works by raising fetal haemoglobin.
